name: Question 10
problem:
Describe the set $S={…,\frac{1}{4},1,4,16,64,...}$ using a constructive definition.

*Hint: Take ${a}_{1}=4$ in the sequence that generates the elements of $S.$*

$$
{4}^{n}
$$
worked_solution:
Notice that the elements of our set

$$
…,\,\frac{1}{4},\,1,\,4,\,16,\,64,\,…
$$

form a two-way infinite geometric sequence with a common ratio $r=4:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =4 \\  & =\frac{(1)}{(\frac{1}{4})} \\  & =\frac{4}{1} \\  & =\frac{16}{4} \\  & =⋯\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, setting  ${a}_{1}=4,$ the $n$th term ${a}_{n}$ of our sequence for $n\in Z$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}\cdot {r}^{n-1} \\  & =4\cdot {4}^{n-1} \\  & =4\cdot {4}^{n}\cdot {4}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{4}{4}\cdot {4}^{n} \\  & ={4}^{n}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can define our set using a constructive definition as follows:

$$
S={{4}^{n}\,:\,n\in Z}
$$

Describe the set S={…,14,1,4,16,64,...} using a constructive definition.

Hint: Take a1=4 in the sequence that generates the elements of S.

EXPLANATION

Notice that the elements of our set …,14,1,4,16,64,… form a two-way infinite geometric sequence with a common ratio r=4:

r=4=(1)(14)=41=164=⋯

Therefore, setting a1=4, the nth term an of our sequence for n∈Z is given by

an=a1⋅rn−1=4⋅4n−1=4⋅4n⋅4−1=44⋅4n=4n.

Therefore, we can define our set using a constructive definition as follows:

S={4n:n∈Z}
